author: Hodgson, 1836
habitat: 민가 주변 야산, 공원, 산림, 사찰 주변
summary: 마을 가까운 야산과 공원, 산림, 절 둘레에 찾아오는 흔하지 않은 여름철새이다. 번식기인 5~6월에는 해 질 녘부터 새벽까지 밤새 울고, 날이 흐리면 낮에도 운다. 나무 구멍에 흰 알을 3~4개 낳으며, 주로 곤충을 잡아먹지만 작은 새나 쥐도 잡는다. 우리나라 전역에 산다.

art.subject: Oriental Scops Owl (Otus sunia), adult grey morph as seen in Korea from May to September: plumage grey-brown, finely vermiculated and flecked with brown and black, the upperparts with dark shaft streaks; prominent erectile ear tufts; greyish facial disc with a fine dark rim; a row of white spots along the scapulars forming a pale line on the folded wing; underparts paler grey with bold black shaft streaks crossed by fine wavy bars. Bill dark grey; iris yellow; legs feathered, toes bare and greyish.
art.pose: perched upright on a branch at dusk, calling
art.scene: Korean wooded hillside near a village in early summer, at dusk; no people, buildings or text
views: adult grey morph, side view perched: grey-brown plumage flecked with brown and black, prominent ear tufts, white scapular line, yellow eyes, bare greyish toes
adult rufous morph, side view perched: bright rufous-brown overall with fewer, finer dark streaks, ear tufts, yellow eyes, bare toes
art.build: Very small, slim owl, about 20cm, about the length of a Common Starling and much smaller and slimmer than the larger scops owl resident in Korea; small head with erectile ear tufts. Bill small and hooked. Legs feathered, toes bare. Wings long and pointed for an owl: at rest the wingtips reach about the tail tip. By day it sits upright and stretched thin against a trunk, looking like a broken stub.
avoid: Do not paint orange-red eyes; Oriental Scops Owl has yellow eyes (orange-red eyes mark the larger resident scops owl).
Do not paint feathered toes; the toes are bare.
Do not paint a pale collar on the hindneck or a bulky body.
Do not paint it as large as a Long-eared Owl or with an orange facial disc.
